requirements.requirement: Add a 512 MiB swap file on node1 and activate it immediately.
requirements.summary: The baseline showed no /swapfile. The executor created a 536,870,912-byte, root-owned mode-0600 swap file and directly observed it in the active swap inventory.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the swap file activates after future boots.
requirements.summary: Exactly one valid /etc/fstab entry was installed. A bounded reboot changed the boot ID, after which the system was running, swapfile.swap was active, and /swapfile remained active with the correct size, signature, permissions, and persistent entry.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. The 512 MiB swap file was active immediately and directly demonstrated to reactivate after a verified reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot identities. Only a minor retained fstab backup detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The final existence of /etc/fstab.infraset-before-swapfile was not separately inventoried; retention is inferred from its successful creation and the complete timeline containing no cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating and securing the swap file, updating fstab, activating swap, and performing the required reboot/persistence test. Post-executor observations showed no failed services, new exposure, or package damage. The only hygiene issue is the safety copy /etc/fstab.infraset-before-swapfile: it supported rollback during validation but was not removed afterward and therefore appears to remain as minor abandoned residue. No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were identified.
